rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so the key uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only single-profile model provides a useful performance baseline. This experiment tests the simplest RNA configuration using PCA and no aggregation or fusion, avoiding confounds from multiprofile, learned encoders, or multimodal fusion. It is the best first use of budget because it establishes a reference point for later comparisons of profile setting, RNA encoder choice, aggregation, and multimodal fusion.

The only completed experiment is an RNA-only, single-profile PCA baseline, so the value of the image modality is still unknown. config_010 is the simplest image-only, single-profile ResNet50 model, testing whether image features alone provide useful signal without introducing aggregation or fusion. This is the best next experiment because it establishes the missing unimodal baseline, reduces uncertainty about a top-level design choice, and creates a reference for later multimodal/fusion comparisons under a limited budget.

RNA-only PCA is much stronger than image-only ResNet, but the weak image result may reflect a poor image encoder rather than the image modality itself. config_013 tests a stronger image representation, ImageNet ViT-L, in the same image-only single-profile setting, so it isolates the effect of image encoder choice. This is the best next experiment because it is a clean comparison that determines whether image features are viable before spending budget on multimodal fusion or more complex image aggregation.

The strongest completed result is RNA-only PCA singleprofile (0.485 acc), while image-only models are much weaker (0.21-0.23 acc), so RNA representation is the promising direction. The key uncertainty is whether using multiple profiles with a simple aggregation improves on the singleprofile RNA baseline. config_002 keeps the same RNA encoder and modality, changing only to multiprofile with avgpool, making it a clean test of profile setting/aggregation. It is a better use of the next budget than adding fusion or changing multiple factors, because it directly clarifies whether multiprofile aggregation is worth pursuing before more complex RNA or multimodal variants.

The strongest result so far is RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool (0.591 accuracy), clearly better than single-profile RNA (0.485) and much better than image-only baselines. The main uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can further improve multiprofile RNA representation. config_003 tests this by changing only aggregation from avgpool to transformer, making it a clean exploitation step that also informs whether transformer aggregation is worth using in later multimodal designs.

The strongest evidence is that RNA-only PCA with multiprofile avgpool is the best configuration so far (0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), while image-only models are much weaker and transformer aggregation is worse than avgpool for PCA. The key remaining uncertainty is whether a learned RNA representation can improve on PCA under this best profile/aggregation setting. config_005 changes only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 while keeping multiprofile and avgpool, isolating the representation effect. It is the best next experiment because RNA is currently the dominant modality, so this has high expected leverage and creates a stronger baseline before testing multimodal fusion.

The strongest evidence is that RNA-only multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation outperform single-profile and transformer-aggregated variants, and scvi_n200 avgpool is currently the best configuration at 0.650 validation accuracy. Image-only models are weak, so multimodal fusion is not yet the most informative next step. config_008 tests scgpt with the same multiprofile + avgpool setup as the current best, isolating the RNA encoder choice. This is a one-factor extension that clarifies whether scgpt can beat scvi_n200 or whether scvi remains the preferred representation, making it a high-value use of the next experiment.

RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 with avgpool is currently the best configuration, but aggregation has only been tested for this encoder with avgpool; transformer was weaker for pca, so it is unclear whether it can help scvi. config_006 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer, directly testing whether a more expressive profile aggregation improves the strongest RNA representation without confounding image modality or fusion. This is an efficient next step because it exploits the best current direction while reducing uncertainty about an important design choice before spending budget on multimodal configurations.

The strongest evidence is RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200, with avgpool and transformer nearly tied (0.650/0.628 vs 0.653/0.628), while image-only models are weak and multimodal fusion is untested. config_030 keeps the best RNA encoder/profile/aggregation from config_005 and adds only resnet50 image features with simple concat fusion, directly testing whether image provides complementary signal to the best RNA baseline. This is the best next use of budget because it exploits the most promising direction with a minimal, interpretable fusion test, and its comparison to config_005/006 will clarify whether multimodality helps or hurts before adding more complex image encoders or fusion schemes.

The strongest evidence is RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 (0.653 acc / 0.628 F1 with transformer, 0.650 / 0.628 with avgpool), while the only multimodal test so far (scvi + resnet50, avgpool, concat) underperforms RNA-only at 0.632 / 0.607. This creates uncertainty about whether the image modality is unhelpful or whether concat fusion is over-weighting a weak image representation. config_031 changes only fusion from concat to weighted in the same multimodal setup, directly testing whether learned weighting can make the image modality useful or confirm that resnet50 image features do not add value. This is a focused, high-information extension of the best RNA encoder/profile setting and avoids changing multiple factors at once.
